title: The card for the flagship chore shows an invoice id and a model-written sentence, not the recipient or the message that will be sent
expected: Action, recipient, rationale and exact parameters, so she can sign what a good bookkeeper would send (character criterion 3; 'show me the invoice and the sentence you will send').
got: ledgerbox's send_reminder takes only {id}; the recipient and body live in a draft the page saved earlier through the AUTO draft_reminder. The card prints action, the model's rationale and params {id: inv_...}. No recipient field exists in CardView, no draft, and capture is hard-coded null (the gate never passes capture_id when it files the card, so even the README's 'screenshot beside the card' cannot arrive). Whether the recipient is visible depends on the model choosing to write it into the rationale, which is untrusted prose.
code_check: Read: CardView has id/action/rationale/params/capture only; cardView() sets capture:null; hooks.py approvals.create() is called without capture_id. ledgerbox send_reminder parameters list is [INVOICE_ID] only. reproduced with a throwaway vitest file outside the repo (T-number in the evidence note); no repo file touched.
suggested_acceptance: A card's recipient and message come from the tool's own params (the page should accept 'to' and 'body' as parameters, or the gate should enrich the card from the READ result of the draft). Until then name the limit in the card footer.
l2_priority: Live ledgerbox on :3001, Claude Code engine, onboarded store, ledgerbox registered. One real turn 'chase invoices over 30 days'. Record exactly what the slip shows for send_reminder and whether recipient and subject appear anywhere without opening Main.

title: A card that arrives while she is put away steals keyboard focus and opens the slip, contradicting 'does not open the slip over the user's work'
expected: Per ADR 0026 'Hide means put away': she returns as her quiet home form with a pink ring and a count, with no slip over the work and no focus change (pet peeve: windows that steal focus mid-typing).
got: The machine asks for the quiet form and then calls athena_show. Rust show() does window.show(), window.set_focus() and emits athena:summon. The page's summon handler recomputes from its own facts, sees a waiting card, clears snoozed, sets mode auto and focuses the Approve button. Executed with a fake Rust that echoes summon: form = slip, snoozed = false, effects: show+set_focus, size:slip, focus:approve. The payload's 'cards' is ignored, so the report/emit race does not rescue it.
code_check: T1 in the scratch vitest: 'T1 form after summon echo: slip snoozed: false size:seal,hide,show+set_focus,size:seal,focus:approve,size:slip'. The Rust half is read, not run (L1). runtime.test.ts uses fakes that never echo summon, which is why the suite is green.
suggested_acceptance: Split Rust show() into show-without-activate (card arrival) and summon (user asked); or make the page ignore athena:summon when it caused the show itself.
l2_priority: Windows 11, Main focused with a text field active and typing, Athena hidden via the tray 'Put Athena away', then trigger one gated card (ledgerbox turn already in flight). Observe: does the foreground window change, does the slip open, do keystrokes land in the field. Needs a real WebView2 foreground state.

title: When she is visible, a card grows her to the 488x316 slip at once, over whatever sits in the bottom-right corner, with no gap between 'she needs me' and 'she covers my work'
expected: Impossible to miss when something needs her, but the person decides when the paper unrolls over a video call or a reply box.
got: formOf returns slip for any waiting, un-snoozed, visible card and finalize() asks Rust for the slip size immediately (growth is sent at once). Her default resting place is 24px from the bottom-right corner of the work area, which is where mail reply boxes and call controls sit. She does not take focus in this path (set_size never activates), so A/D typed into the other app do not answer the card; the chord is the only no-focus answer.
code_check: T1b: 'T1b form: slip size:seal,size:slip' (visible, no hide). Enumerated every state size in T4.
suggested_acceptance: Accept if the owner wants interruption by design; otherwise the slip should open as the home form with ring and count and open only on a click or the chord.
l2_priority: Two real monitors or one, a typing session in a browser at bottom-right, card arrives. Measure what the slip occludes and whether typing continues uninterrupted. Env: Windows, fresh store, non-first launch so she rests bottom-right.

title: Approve is optimistic: the card is dropped and the stamp says 'Approved. Stamped and sent to the record.' before the daemon answers, and a refusal leaves no card and no visible error
expected: A stamp means the daemon accepted the answer. A refusal (foreign_origin, expired, daemon down) keeps the card or says so where she is looking.
got: run.answer filters the card out of the store first, then POSTs /decisions/<id> with the origin of whichever tab is focused NOW. The daemon refuses an origin whose session is pinned to a different app (403 foreign_origin), so answering a ledgerbox card while the hirelane or tidycrm tab is in front fails. The store sets phase=error and the card is gone. The machine's work flag never toggles (error is not 'running'), so there is no tape line; the only place the error shows is Talk in the expanded ledger. The screen-reader line and the stamp have already said 'Approved'. The daemon row stays pending (24h) and is never re-offered (see mira-5).
code_check: T5: 'cards: 0 phase: error error: foreign_origin ... pinned to host:hirelane and this card belongs to host:ledgerbox'. T7: after approve then cards->0 the machine settles at form 'seal', lingering false (the failure never reaches the tape). The routes.py refusal is read, not run.
suggested_acceptance: Send the card's own origin (card.origin, already on the wire) instead of the focused tab's; keep the card until the daemon answers 2xx; show a 'not sent' state on the slip.
l2_priority: Register ledgerbox and hirelane, file a ledgerbox card, switch Main to the hirelane tab, press Approve. Expect a visible refusal; the L1 reading predicts a silent drop. Env: two registered origins, daemon ready.

title: A waiting decision does not survive a restart, a Clear click, or closing Main: nothing ever reads GET /decisions back into the UI
expected: 'Hiding does not make me miss a waiting decision' and a card waits up to 24h in the daemon (DEFAULT_TTL), so the surface should re-offer what the daemon still holds.
got: DaemonApi.decisions() has zero callers outside its own definition. Cards exist only as decision.requested events inside the window's own /run stream. The ledger's Clear button runs run.clear(), which empties cards (executed: 'T6 cards after clear: 0') without declining them. Closing Main exits the whole app (lib.rs close handler), killing the daemon sidecar; the approval rows persist. The next turn's frame still tells the model the card is waiting (pending_lines), so the model can say 'waiting on your approval' about a card she can no longer see.
code_check: grep -rn 'decisions()' apps/desktop/src -> only the definition. T6 confirms Clear drops cards. Wiring ratio entry: DaemonApi.decisions 0/1 callers.
suggested_acceptance: On daemon ready and on every restart call decisions() and seed the run store's cards; make Clear refuse while cards wait, or decline them explicitly.
l2_priority: File a card, press Clear in her Talk tab, then check /decisions (pending) vs the UI; separately quit and relaunch with a pending card. Env: onboarded store, one real GATED turn.

title: Main's close button is labelled 'Close Main window. Athena stays.' but closing Main quits the whole app, Athena and the daemon included
expected: The accessible name and the behaviour agree; closing Main leaves her running (J5 definition of done: 'close it knowing what happens to her').
got: app.tsx:134 gives the button aria-label 'Close Main window. Athena stays.'. lib.rs:303-305 handles CloseRequested on Main with handle.exit(0), with a comment saying the opposite of the label. Any pending card is lost (mira-5). The label is a false statement of the product's own behaviour.
code_check: Read twice: label string and handler. No test asserts either.
suggested_acceptance: Either change the label to 'Quit Athena' or hide Main instead of exiting; ADR 0026 does not record the choice, which also needs an ADR (AGENTS: one decision, one ADR).
l2_priority: Press X on Main with the slip open and a card waiting; observe the process list and whether her window and tray vanish. Env: Windows, any onboarded store.

title: The global chord approves the first waiting card even when the card is not on screen (slip put away with Esc, or her window hidden from the tray)
expected: A chord answers a card the person has just seen. The brief says the chord exists 'only for the moment a person is being asked something'.
got: Chords are registered as soon as cards > 0, regardless of whether the slip is open. decide fires the answer effect immediately and only then draws the stamp. Executed: after esc the form is 'seal' (badge 1), then chord approve -> 'answer:approval_1:approve' is sent. A tray 'Put Athena away' never tells the page (nothing dispatches hide), so machine.hidden stays false and the chord answers an invisible window.
code_check: T2: 'T2 after esc form: seal' then 'T2 log: size:seal,size:slip,answer:approval_1:approve,size:slip'.
suggested_acceptance: A chord with no visible card should first summon the slip (second press answers), or require the slip to have been shown in the last N seconds.
l2_priority: File a card, press Esc on the slip, press Ctrl+Alt+A while another app is focused. Confirm what is sent. Env: Windows, chord not owned by another app.

title: 'Answerable by keyboard in one key without opening Main' is only true when her window already has focus; the no-focus path is a three-key chord that the UI never mentions
expected: The slip says how to answer from wherever she is typing, and a chord that cannot register says so.
got: A and D are window-level key handlers (live.tsx:184-189) and only fire with her focused; with the slip showing over another app they type into that app. Ctrl+Alt+A / Ctrl+Alt+D are the only focus-free answer. The strings Ctrl+Alt+A and Ctrl+Alt+D appear in no view, tooltip or aria text (grep over src: 0 hits); the slip rail shows only kbd A and D. A refused registration (another app owns the chord) is eprintln! only. On layouts where Ctrl+Alt is AltGr (Polish, others) the registered chord also swallows AltGr+A / AltGr+D typing for as long as a card waits.
code_check: grep -rn 'Ctrl+Alt' apps/desktop/src -> 0 hits in UI sources. Handler read twice.
suggested_acceptance: Show 'Ctrl+Alt+A / D from anywhere' on the slip and the pill tooltip; surface a failed registration in the slip.
l2_priority: With another app focused, press A then Ctrl+Alt+A on the live slip; with the chord pre-registered by another tool, check whether any message appears. Env: Windows, a keyboard layout with AltGr (e.g. Polish) for the typing side effect.

title: The welcome names the engine with a tick but never probes it; the Setup engine row says 'the probe has not answered' forever
expected: J1 definition of done: the engine is named and found, or the user is told plainly what is missing and how to fix it.
got: Welcome prints 'Engine: <settings.engine>' with a green check icon unconditionally; the value is the stored setting (default claude_code), not a probe. Setup passes probes: null with a comment that nothing asks the daemon yet. harness/engines.py has probe()/probe_all() but routes.py exposes no probe route (routes: health, manifest, run, decisions, ledger, playbooks, ...). For Mira (Claude Code present) the tick happens to be true; a missing or signed-out CLI would still show the tick and the failure would first appear as a turn error.
code_check: grep -n probe src/athena/daemon/routes.py -> no route. Welcome check icon has no conditional.
suggested_acceptance: Expose probe_all over a daemon route and gate the tick on state 'found'; render 'not found / not signed in' with the remedy text that already exists in lib/engines.ts.
l2_priority: Fresh store on a host with Claude Code present (Mira) and, as a control, with the claude binary renamed. Read the welcome text in both.

title: 'Later (Esc)' on first launch leaves Main hidden, onboarded false and no control in her window that opens Main; the tray menu is the only way
expected: Later defers the app choice without losing the product (J1 'what Later (Esc) does').
got: On first launch Main is built hidden. Later/Esc only flips her mode to auto: she becomes a seal at ~22% of the screen height; the Talk tab is blocked ('Open a page first') and no tab exists. No view in her window offers 'Open Main' (grep 'Main' in views.tsx: 0). The Main window appears only through the tray item 'Show Main window' (tray.rs:135,146-149) or by completing Open your first app. onboarded stays false, so the next launch shows the welcome again.
code_check: Read: reducer branches 'later' and 'esc' for mode welcome only change mode; no onboard effect.
suggested_acceptance: Give the resting seal a 'Open Main' action when Main is hidden, or have Later show Main on the Browser module.
l2_priority: Fresh store, press Later, then try to reach Main using only visible affordances; note whether the tray icon is in the overflow area (Windows 11 default).

title: The per-app 'Switch off' / 'Disable' control and the pinned-class overrides are display-only: nothing in the daemon, the run loop or the bridge reads them
expected: 'The gate is the policy' (AGENTS.md): a standing user switch stops that origin from acting on the next call (policy.py rule 2 says exactly this).
got: The enabled flag and overrides are written to the shell's origins table and rendered on the Browser ledger ('Switch off') and in her Origins tab ('Disable', 'N pinned'). Their only consumers are display code. The daemon's Policy has a disabled_origins argument, but wiring.py builds Policy(connectors=vault) / Policy() and never passes it. So 'off' is a word, and a user who switches ledgerbox off to be safe is not safe.
code_check: grep -rn disabled_origins src -> definition and use inside policy.py only. grep '\.enabled' over apps/desktop/src (non-test) -> display sites and the register action only.
suggested_acceptance: Pass the shell's disabled origins to the daemon (a store read or a header on /run), then add a test that a switched-off origin's call is refused foreign_origin.
l2_priority: Register ledgerbox, switch it off in Browser or Origins, run 'what can you do on this page' and then a gated chase. Expect refusal; the L1 reading predicts the turn proceeds. Env: ledgerbox on :3001, daemon ready.

title: Her default resting spot is inside the edge-snap zone, so the first small nudge turns her into a 28px tab
expected: A drag of a few pixels leaves her where she was dropped; docking is a deliberate throw to an edge.
got: Non-first launches place the seal 24px from the work area's right and bottom edges. classify() snaps to ScreenRight when the gap is <= SNAP_PX (32). Executed arithmetic: gap 24 <= 32, so any drop near the default position docks. A tab is 28x96 with no label (the caption is hidden in tab), and a docked tab hides the seal until clicked.
code_check: python arithmetic: 'default seal x 1820 distance to right edge 24 snaps ScreenRight on any nudge: True'. Rust tests (a_seal_at_a_screen_edge_docks) assert the classifier, not the default placement.
suggested_acceptance: Place the default outside the snap band (>= 48px) or require a drag past the band to dock.
l2_priority: Drag the resting seal 10px left and release at 100/125/150% scaling; observe whether she docks. Env: non-first-launch store.

title: There is no way to put her away from her own window; the machine's hide event is never dispatched
expected: J2 'put her away': a visible control or key, and a first-launch hint of where the tray is.
got: Search: the machine event {t:'hide'} and athenaHide have no dispatcher in live.tsx or views.tsx; the only hide paths are the tray menu 'Put Athena away' and Alt+F4 on her focused window (CloseRequested -> hide). On Windows 11 new tray icons sit in the overflow flyout by default, so the way back (tray click or Ctrl+Shift+Space) is the only recovery path and Ctrl+Shift+Space is not printed anywhere in the UI either.
code_check: grep -rn '"hide"|athenaHide' apps/desktop/src -> definition, type and runtime dispatch of the effect only; no event source.
suggested_acceptance: Add Put away to the ledger header and print Ctrl+Shift+Space on the welcome.
l2_priority: Windows 11, fresh install: is the tray icon pinned or in overflow; time to find Put Athena away and to bring her back.

title: Main starts at a fixed 1440x900 logical and nothing clamps it to the work area, so at 125% and 150% scaling it opens larger than the screen and her dock beside it slides over Main
expected: First launch lands on a usable window at the user's scaling (character: 100/125/150%).
got: build_shell uses inner_size(1440, 900) and .center() with no work-area check. Logical work areas (arithmetic): 1920x1080 at 125% -> 1536x824 (fails on height), at 150% -> 1280x688 (fails on both). companion::place() then slides her rectangle the least distance into the work area, which puts the seal over Main's right edge instead of beside it.
code_check: python arithmetic over three scale factors (output in the review). The WebView2 reaction to an oversized inner_size is not run (L1).
suggested_acceptance: Clamp initial size to 90% of the monitor work area; add a test.
l2_priority: Windows display at 125% and 150% on a 1920x1080 panel, fresh store, Open your first app. Screenshot the whole screen and report whether Main's title bar and Athena's seal are fully on screen.

title: 37 overdue invoices become 37 single-card decisions with no batch, and each answer holds the slip for 1.5s while presses are silently dropped
expected: Net saving of at least 25 minutes over 45 manual (criterion 6) for the monthly chase.
got: ledgerbox's seed has 37 invoices more than 30 days past due (README line 24). Each send is its own GATED card. After a decision the machine ignores further decide events until the settle timer (TEAR 900ms, SETTLE 1500ms, JS constants that ignore prefers-reduced-motion). A held-down Ctrl+Alt+A therefore answers one card per 1.5s and drops the rest without feedback. There is no 'approve the rest that match' action. The cards also carry no recipient (mira-1), so signing 37 means either 37 blind approvals or 37 trips to the page.
code_check: Read: 'if (s.decided || shown(s) === 0) return;' at machine.ts:279. Estimate derivation is in the review.
suggested_acceptance: Accept the one-card-per-decision rule (it is the gate's design) but state the cost; consider a 'review all' list view.
l2_priority: Time one full chase of the seeded 37 on ledgerbox with a stopwatch, both ways: reading each draft in the page, and approving from the slip only.

title: The card does not say which app it belongs to, and most of the card's wire fields never reach a view
expected: With several tabs open she can tell a ledgerbox send from a hirelane or tidycrm act at a glance, and sees when the card expires.
got: DecisionRequested has 11 wire fields; the slip draws 4 (id in an aria-label, action, rationale, params). origin, expires_at, decision_kind, surface, capture_id and options (beyond the id lookup) are never rendered, so the app is visible only if it is part of the action name 'host:ledgerbox.send_reminder' (truncated with an ellipsis in a 13px mono cell). RunState.tools, CompanionModel.talk.ready, Snap.to and Summon.cards are other computed values with zero view uses.
code_check: Wiring audit by script (see review): top-level CompanionModel 27/27 used, leaf fields 38/39 (talk.ready 0); DecisionRequested 4/11 reach a view; Rust events 10/10 listened, 2 payload fields ignored; 5/15 component files have no importer (EmptyState, Facts, PageSection, PushToTalk, Table).
suggested_acceptance: Render the origin chip and the expiry on the slip; delete or use the five orphan components.
l2_priority: Slip with a long action name at 125% scaling: is the app still readable; two cards from two origins in the queue.

title: The Browser module's registered-apps ledger (standing, hands, tool counts, Switch on/off) is covered by the page while any tab is open; the strip shows only 'N tools'
expected: J5: see 'this page offers N tools' and whether she has hands or tools there, with the apps ledger one click away.
got: With the Browser module selected and a tab focused, layout.rs clips the chrome webview to the 76px bar+strip and a native page webview fills the rest, so the ledger body (view.tsx:61-106) is drawn under the page. The strip's pill says '3 tools', '0 tools' or 'no bridge'; the sentence about hands ('The generic hands are how it is operated') lives in the page-stand-in block that the page covers. Her own Origins tab does list offers and enable toggles, so the information is reachable, but via a different window.
code_check: Read twice (layout.rs rects() and the view).
suggested_acceptance: Add 'hands' to the strip pill text when count is 0 and the origin is enabled.
l2_priority: Open ledgerbox (N tools) and a site with no WebMCP (0 tools). Report what the strip says and where she finds out hands exist.

title: 'Never sent twice' rests on the model not proposing the same send again; the gate dedupes a card id, not an invoice
expected: A second chase of an invoice already chased today either does not file a card or the card says 'reminded 2 days ago'.
got: approvals.resolve refuses a second answer to one card, so a double click or two chords cannot double-send (strength). A fresh turn that proposes send_reminder for the same invoice files a new card; the card shows no prior-send fact, and the daemon's dedupe is the model reading pending_decisions in its frame. Page-side behaviour (ledgerbox's reminder count) is not part of the card.
code_check: Read only; whether ledgerbox itself refuses a repeat send was not exercised.
suggested_acceptance: Mention in the gate docs that idempotence per invoice is the host's job.
l2_priority: Chase the same invoice in two turns and approve both; record what ledgerbox does and what the second card shows.

title: Long parameters scroll inside the 316px slip but the scroll region is not keyboard focusable and carries no 'more below' cue
expected: The exact parameters can be read completely by keyboard (criterion 3 'exact parameters'), and the slip says when more is below.
got: The slip's .sl-scroll is overflow-y:auto with a focus-visible style but the element has no tabIndex (the ledger's lg-scroll has tabIndex 0). A long fill value from a generic hand (page_fill text) wraps (overflow-wrap:anywhere) and pushes later parameters out of sight. No (showing N of M) because nothing is cut, but the user cannot tell the list continues.
code_check: Read twice; not rendered (L1).
suggested_acceptance: Add tabIndex=0 and a bottom fade or 'n more' hint.
l2_priority: A card with five parameters, one 600-character; press Tab and see whether the parameter list takes focus; also at 150% scaling.

title: Sizes, the anchor arithmetic and the 'at rest' footprint are owned by Rust and match the character's bar
expected: At rest at most 100x100 and she does not take focus (criterion 2).
got: STATES is a Rust table the page can only name; seal is 92x92 including the 8px shadow margin (drawn 76), tab is 28x96, every other state is larger and only on a card, work, listening, welcome or ledger. Rust tests assert that growing never moves the seal in any orientation and that placement flips or slides to stay in the work area. At rest she does not call set_focus; the only focus grabs are launch (lib.rs:215), the tray/chord/pill summon and mira-2.
code_check: T4 enumerated all 7 states: seal 92x92 and tab 28x96 are <=100; tape, hear, slip, welcome, ledger are larger by design. vitest: 22 files / 206 tests pass.
suggested_acceptance: n/a (strength)
l2_priority: Real pixel measurement of the seal window at 100/125/150% scaling and a focus-stealing check at rest for ten minutes.

title: Legibility holds: nothing is under 12px and every reading pair measured is at or above 4.87:1; the companion is theme-fixed so both themes read identically
expected: Nothing she must read is under 12px; both themes readable (criterion 5).
got: A scan of every CSS font size/shorthand found the minimum at exactly 12px (labels, kbd, captions) and none below; no root font-size override. Measured contrast: paper ink 16.9, ink-2 7.0 on paper and 5.6 on paper-3, stamp pink 7.0, white on stamp 7.9, white on primary 5.4, house ink 10.0 and the waiting caption 7.1 on the housing, badge ink on pink 7.2. The lowest are the green 'ok' ink 4.9 and the disabled Speak button at 2.1 (opacity .45; disabled controls are exempt, but it is always disabled when no voice backend exists, so the dead button is permanently low-contrast). Main follows the settings row via store:changed.
code_check: python contrast script and a regex over every .css (output in the review). 12px is the floor, so a user at 100% on a 4K panel will find the 12px labels small.
suggested_acceptance: n/a (strength)
l2_priority: Screenshots at 100/125/150% in both OS themes; read the 12px labels at arm's length.

title: Declining is as cheap as approving and is recorded where it counts: the daemon writes an episode and a user_denied ledger row
expected: Decline is as easy as approve and is recorded (criterion 4).
got: D, the Decline button and Ctrl+Alt+D take the same path as approve (same decide event, same stamp, same 1.5s). The daemon's answer_decision on a decline appends '[decision] the user declined ...' as an episode and writes a ledger row with reason user_denied; the window's Record tab lists the session's decisions. The session list is in memory and the Record tab's daemon half shows model calls, so a decline is not shown after a restart (the daemon holds it).
code_check: Read; the lane half is covered by existing Python tests (not rerun at L1).
suggested_acceptance: n/a (strength)
l2_priority: Decline one card, restart the app, look for the decline in the Record tab and in /ledger.
